claims.text: The starting eutectic AlCoCrFeNi alloy has a lamellar microstructure comprising FCC and BCC phases.
Post-solidification aging at approximately 500°C for 2–4 hours can be optimized to improve the alloy.
An inert or vacuum atmosphere is suitable for the proposed aging treatment.
Performing the treatment immediately after controlled solidification will maintain the lamellar microstructure.
Varying aging temperature from 450°C to 550°C and duration from 2 to 6 hours can identify conditions that avoid over-aging.
Optimized aging will form ultrafine, coherent B2 nanoprecipitates.
The B2 nanoprecipitates will be uniformly distributed within the softer FCC matrix.
B2 nanoprecipitates will obstruct dislocation motion through Orowan strengthening.
Local strain fields induced by the precipitates will promote more uniform plastic deformation.
More uniform plastic deformation will reduce strain localization and improve ductility.
Optimized aging will increase yield strength by 20–30% relative to the as-solidified alloy.
Optimized aging will improve ductility by 10–15% relative to the as-solidified alloy.
Departures from the optimal temperature, time, or atmosphere may cause precipitate coarsening or structural degradation and eliminate the property improvements.
Variations in local composition or processing can alter precipitate size distribution and mechanical properties.
